| B9.5 · Metering — the one credit charge path (`charge()`, idempotent) | 🔨 this PR (branch `claude/console-bold-port-b95-ub92fj`) — the money unit, taken as SLICE 1 of 2 on the spec's own rule that correctness beats coverage. **Built**: `charge()` in `packages/db` (it needs a Prisma transaction; the price RULE stays pure in core), the reveal as its FIRST caller with its inlined `resolveCreditPrice` copy and hard-coded `?? 1` deleted, `sourceType`/`sourceId`/`meta` on `CreditLedger` behind a PARTIAL unique index in raw SQL (Prisma cannot express one — the `BusinessContext` workaround), `refundCharge()` writing a compensating positive row so the ledger stays append-only, and the drift guard MOVED to the new seam. **The crux (§3) is proven**: a replay, a retry and five concurrent attempts on one source leave exactly one row; the insert is `createMany({skipDuplicates})` because in Postgres a unique violation ABORTS the transaction, so insert-and-catch would hand the caller a poisoned tx. Zero-priced writes nothing; unpriced writes nothing and says so distinctly rather than inventing a number. **Deferred to slice 2, stated not dropped**: the channel charge points (email, SMS, calls, enrichment) and §5's slow-don't-stop, because charging a send without the pre-check means a message goes out that cannot be paid for — that pairing IS §5, not an addition to it. `NOT METERED YET` therefore does not shrink yet, and the B3c-1 call-sheet line stays as it is, so the two surfaces still agree. Validation, all UNCACHED (§7.13): build 25/25 · lint · test 50/50 · api 315/315 incl. `metering-charge.e2e.spec.ts` 10/10. DEC-157..160; Qs 150–159. **Approved by the owner as slice 1 (2026-09-01)**, with the split ruled correct — §5 is a PRECONDITION of metering sends, not an addition to it. Slice 2 is the send/SMS/dial/enrich meters + §5 whole (pre-check, urgency split, hold release) + §6's copy shrink, in one PR. DEC-160 records the two process rules from the same ruling, and Q-155 is re-marked LAUNCH-GATING and owner-owned. |

| DEC-110  | 2026-08-26 | **B2.6 — Suggested campaigns (closes Q-066).** **(1) A suggestion IS a draft campaign.** The owner's ruling made literal: the sweep writes a DRAFT `Agent` row through the ONE create path (`agentCreateData` — extracted so `POST /agents` and the sweep assemble the identical shape; no parallel proposal schema), carrying an additive `Agent.suggestion Json?` marker (core `agentSuggestionSchema`: signal · reason · count · at · dismissedAt?). Refusal strings are written for a stranger: they never name a tenant, an id, or confirm what exists. **(4) Attribution is a plan check, never a toggle.** Agency tier → that tier's `Plan.features.whiteLabel`. `FeatureFlag` was rejected on purpose: it is workspace-scoped and would hand a workspace user exactly the switch canon §7 forbids. An unresolved plan SHOWS the line — the failure mode must be 'Clientforce is credited'. Both directions are e2e'd, including that a plan row for a DIFFERENT tier grants nothing. **(5) The server advertises only what it can serve.** W1 implements `askQuestion`; a workspace with all six enabled still gets one chip, and `quick_action` on an unbuilt flow is refused. `capture_submit` is refused outright — accepting a bag of PII with nowhere to put it is worse than refusing. **(6) Grounded or silent.** Retrieval via `@clientforce/knowledge`, composition via the `@clientforce/ai` gateway with a prompt that refuses to invent; `AiTask` gains `widget` (the union's own comment anticipated it) on the fast tier at 400 tokens. With no completion provider the endpoint returns AGENT_UNAVAILABLE — the API process ships an embeddings-only gateway, so this is the honest state in CI and in any environment without keys. **(7)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | **SPEC A — on-call contact awareness: the agent READS THE RECORD mid-call through a tool, instead of being prompt-stuffed once _(Id history: claimed DEC-094 at dispatch vs then-main `9d42100` — STALE. Main had already advanced: the WID unit merged as `a197ae2` and, after its own renumber chain (094→096→097), landed DEC-097 + Q-049/Q-050; 094/095 are held by #108's W2/W3 and 096 by INT W4. Renumbered to **DEC-099 / Q-051** at the owner's ruling and re-verified against live main `7b97e18` — collision-free: no DEC-099 or Q-051 anywhere in that tree.)_ (1) **A TOOL, not a bigger prompt.** The whole contact history does not ride the system prompt. The brain gets ONE tool, `lookup_contact_context`, and calls it per question: question → scoped lookup → grounded answer. Stuffing scales with the record and poisons every turn's latency and salience; a per-question lookup costs nothing on the turns that don't need one. (2) **FIVE facets, one store each** — `history` (past replies/threads) · `pipeline` (stage + campaign membership) · `bookings` (prior calls/outcomes + booked-stage moves) · `profile` (tags/notes/custom fields) · `knowledge` (the P1.2 RAG corpus). Each maps to a distinct question a caller actually asks; a sixth is a vocabulary decision, never a silent widening. The spec's three worked examples land on three different facets by construction (pricing → knowledge, "we spoke before?" → history, reschedule → bookings). (3) **HONEST ABSENCE IS STRUCTURAL, not a prompt plea.** `found:false` is a first-class result carrying a speakable note; `renderRecallResult` turns it into an explicit "NOTHING ON RECORD … do not guess", and a REFUSED lookup renders "NOT AVAILABLE" instead — because "we looked and found nothing" and "we could not look" are different claims and the agent must be able to make the right one. composer.voice@v2 rule 9 spells out what to say when the record is silent: a model told only "don't invent" still reaches for a plausible answer under conversational pressure. (4) **A RECEIPT PER LOOKUP** on the call record (`CallRetrieval`, additive, append-only, RLS) — facet, the model's own phrasing verbatim, found/empty/refused, item count, latency, provenance ids (never the retrieved bodies). Empty and refused rows are KEPT: an honest "I don't have that on record" is only auditable if the empty lookup left a trace, and a turn with no receipt was answered from the brief alone — that absence is itself the signal. Buffered + flushed at finalize (persistTranscript precedent, idempotent on (callId,seq)) rather than written mid-call: the DEC-092 pacing work exists because the audio path is where jitter becomes audible. Trade stated: a process that dies before finalize loses its receipts exactly as it already loses its transcript. (5) **BOUNDED, always.** 2 lookups/turn · 12/call · 1.5s per lookup · 2 tool ROUNDS, and the final round is sent WITHOUT the tool so the loop must end in an answer. Every bound produces a typed refusal, never a throw — a store error costs the answer, never the call (hardened in-PR after a throwing lookup was found ending calls via respond()'s provider-failure catch). (6) **LATENCY IS MASKED HONESTLY.** A lookup turn pays an extra round trip, so the constant `VOICE_LOOKUP_ACK_LINE` ("Let me check that for you.") fills the gap — spoken ONLY when the model went straight to the tool, silent when it said its own lead-in, and NEVER counted as reply TTFA (the P3.1 ack-clip rule). Metrics report `ttfaByLookup` split: blending a structurally-slower lookup turn into the pooled percentiles would quietly move the numbers the DEC-089 gate is stated in. (7) **SPOKEN-REGISTER SANITIZATION AT THE BOUNDARY.** Retrieved text is stripped of URLs (→ "(a link)", a fact the agent can offer to text over — never a silent deletion), emails, markdown and emoji BEFORE it reaches the model, because the per-sentence voice checks would otherwise refuse a turn for faithfully quoting the record. Pinned against the real checks. (8) **ADDITIVE EVERYWHERE.** Gateway tools absent ⇒ no `tools` field on the wire; recall absent ⇒ composer.voice@v1 byte-identical and the pre-DEC-099 single-stream turn loop — the cert/demo rigs run with no database and must keep producing exactly what DEC-089 certified. Both pinned as identities. (9) **ONE summary event**, `voice.context_retrieved.v1`, per call rather than per lookup (the P5-W1 transitions-only stance; the receipt ledger is the detail). `empty` is the product signal worth having: a caller asked something the record could not answer. (10) **⭑ AUTOMATION-VOCABULARY RIDE-ALONG — `call_knowledge_gap` REGISTERED (owner-approved 2026-07-26).** One new R1 trigger kind on the SHARED vocabulary (core union → matcher → picker, zero picker code): fires off `voice.context_retrieved.v1` when `emptyFacets` is non-empty, with an optional facet narrowing. **ONE firing per call, never per lookup** — the Q-031 mass-fire concern applied up front, and it falls out of the summary-event shape rather than needing a throttle. **A REFUSED lookup is deliberately NOT a gap**: a timeout means the record was never read and may well hold the answer, so reporting it would send the owner to Train Agent to fill a hole that does not exist (pinned at both the metrics source and the matcher). It lights up the canon's "Voice & calls" picker group, whose entries were ALL honest-absent until now — and the five that remain absent had their reason corrected from "Arrives with voice campaigns" (false the moment voice shipped and a voice trigger went live beside them) to "Arrives with call-outcome triggers" / "Arrives with answering-machine detection", regression-pinned. **Q-032 stays OPEN and is NOT closed** — call-outcome triggers need outcome classification (P3.2 call tools); this unit adds none. The Train-Agent half of the loop is Q-051, now SPECIFIED rather than open-ended (owner routing spec, 2026-07-26): a call-detected gap lands in Train Agent as a pre-populated UNGRADED row — verbatim question · the honest-absence line the agent actually spoke (read from the TRANSCRIPT, joined to the receipt on `meta.callId` — never reconstructed from the receipt) · empty-facet source chips · a `☎ from a live call` provenance tag — flowing into the EXISTING grade → teach → note/document path, writing back to knowledge exactly as a manual correction does, and counting toward readiness like any other question. Every field it needs already exists on `CallRetrieval` + the transcript; only the surface is missing. Prompt-stuffing a full history is the failure mode this replaces: it does not scale with the record, it costs latency on every turn including the ones that need nothing, and it makes ungroundedness invisible. A per-question lookup with a receipt makes the agent's knowledge legible after the fact — and makes an honest "I don't have that" provable rather than merely claimed. (1) **Health = a pure, documented formula from ledger aggregates** (`packages/channels/src/health.ts`): 7-day window, weighted components bounce .40 / spam .35 / delivery .15 / reply .10, zero-points at 2× the DEC-019 breach levels (bounce 6%, spam 0.2%); delivery excluded + weights renormalized when no delivery signal exists (missing webhook instrumentation must never read as failure); **sample floor = F1's `SIGNAL_MIN_SENDS`** (<20 sends → NO score, state `low_data`, never gated — statistical honesty, and a fresh sender can always earn a sample); auto-pause below **40**, recovery at **≥55** (hysteresis 40–54 holds the prior state); SMS senders score on their channel twins (`sms.failed` ≈ bounce, `sms.opted_out` ≈ complaint). (b) Bands → healthy ≥80 · warming/watch 60–79 · at-risk 40–59 · auto-pause <40; `<40` is the SHARP `SENDER_UNHEALTHY` threshold — the four-band model REPLACES the 40–54/55 hysteresis (at-risk is a sendable watch zone; W2's ring states = these bands, snapshot gains `band`). (c) Warmup curve → v2, an ABSOLUTE schedule as config TABLES: day 1 = 50/day, ~doubling every ~3 days through week 2 (50→100→250→500→1,000), then linear to 10,000 by day 45; effective cap = min(curve, dailyLimit) unchanged. (d) NEW health interlock: a complaint/bounce spike (rate at/over its danger bound) mid-warmup HOLDS the ramp — the effective day freezes (`warmupState.holdStartedAt`/`heldMs`, deterministic from the row), resumes when the spike clears, completion shifts by the held time; applied by the sweep AND the webhook fast path; hold-on-spike pinned in integration. Every fixture matrix regenerated; band boundaries pinned exactly (80/79/60/59/40/39). #42 #43 #44 + this PR).** The B1 degraded banner stayed up after #39 because five independent faults stacked, each invisible until the previous one cleared: **①** the platform team's network lockdown closed the path to Azure Redis (both containers `connect ETIMEDOUT`; platform-fixed, incl. the storage account in the same sweep) · **②** `redisOptionsFromUrl` dropped the `rediss://` scheme — plain host/port sent plaintext BullMQ connections to a TLS-only 6380 (PR #41; same PR un-redded `infra/scripts/smoke.sh`, which had asserted the pre-C2.1 "Welcome back" dashboard since PR #33 — five red deploys were burying the real outage; the e2e sign-in had the same stale assertion, PR #43) · **③** the #41 regression test's credential-shaped literal tripped the deploy-gating secret-scan (PR CI doesn't run the scan; deploys do) — the scanner was RIGHT, the fixture was wrong; tests now build credentialed URLs at runtime via URL setters (PR #42) · **④** the live cache is Redis CLUSTER: BullMQ's multi-key Lua scripts died with CROSSSLOT until every Queue/Worker passed the hash-tagged `BULL_PREFIX = "{cf}"` (PR #44) · **⑤** WHATWG `URL.password` returns the PERCENT-ENCODED form and Redis AUTH wants the raw secret — an access key ending `=` was sent as `%3D`, so every BullMQ connection looped WRONGPASS while the heartbeat client (ioredis's own decoding URL parser) stayed green: health said "worker alive", yet the API's enqueue hung each doc upload to the 240s ingress timeout (504 "stream timeout"). Fix (this PR): `decodeURIComponent` on username/password in `redisOptionsFromUrl`, and the three local `connectionFrom` copies in knowledge/context/planner queues (same raw-password bug, plus missing SNI) now delegate to it — ONE URL parser platform-wide, with a runtime-built `%3D`→`=` regression test. **Security:** a diagnostic probe run echoed api-container stderr (ioredis error objects include the AUTH argument) into a public-repo Actions log, exposing the encoded Redis key; the run's logs were deleted within minutes but the key is treated as COMPROMISED — platform team must rotate it and update KV `REDIS-URL` after this fix deploys (decoding makes the new key's encoding irrelevant). The probe's two container-log steps now mask token-shaped strings (24+ secret-alphabet chars → `[REDACTED]`) before anything reaches stdout; `worker-health-probe.yml` keeps the storage-target + timed-upload instrumentation as a permanent dispatchable ops tool                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | **Layer ⑥ — cluster-aware Redis clients (`REDIS_CLUSTER=true`).** The post-decode probe proved AUTH fixed (the enqueue Lua actually executed) and surfaced the next fault in ~1s instead of a 240s hang: `ReplyError: MOVED 4633 <node-ip>:8501` → HTTP 500 on upload. The staging cache is **OSS-cluster-policy**: the keyspace is sharded across nodes, a standalone ioredis client cannot follow MOVED redirects, and BullMQ only speaks cluster when handed a **`Cluster` instance** — plain connection options always construct a standalone client (verified in bullmq 5.79 `RedisConnection`). Fix: `bullConnectionFromUrl` in `@clientforce/events` returns plain options normally and a `Redis.Cluster` instance when `REDIS_CLUSTER` is set (explicit flag, not sniffed: a standalone client on a cluster fails only per-key, a cluster client on plain Redis fails outright — guessing wrong is a silent split-brain); Azure OSS-cluster TLS recipe baked in (identity `dnsLookup` — shard nodes are announced by raw IP — and SNI pinned to the cache hostname); `createRedisClient` (heartbeat) is cluster-aware under the same flag so health keeps exercising the same path as the work (DEC-051 lesson); ALL 9 Queue/Worker sites + both EventBus constructions + the channels URL-defaults route through the one factory; `infra/main.bicep` sets `REDIS_CLUSTER=true` on api AND worker (must agree, or one side's queue writes land where the other can't read).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | **A3 follow-up — the Clerk-enabled deploy broke the dev rail (post-#53 staging smoke red: authenticated GET /agents → 307).** Two defects, one fix PR. (1) In Clerk mode `clerkMiddleware` guarded EVERY request, so smoke's and the staging e2e suite's `cf_session` bounced to sign-in. The web now mirrors the api's dual verifier: a request carrying `cf_session` rides the legacy guard — and `bearerToken()` returns the dev token — ONLY while no Clerk browser session exists (`__client_uat*` cookies all absent/zero), so a stale dev cookie can never shadow a real Clerk sign-in into a redirect loop. (2) `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` was runtime-only env (Bicep), but Next.js inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` into the client bundle at BUILD time — the browser half of the app stayed Clerk-blind. The deploy now passes it as a docker build-arg to the web image, gated on the SAME all-four-secrets probe as Bicep's `clerkSecretsAvailable` so image and infra always agree (the publishable key is public-by-design — it ships to every browser — and is masked in run logs regardless). **Second fix PR (same DEC):** the middleware fix exposed a third defect — the api's verifier factory was EITHER/OR (`AUTH_JWKS_URL` set → OIDC only), so with Clerk env live every dev-token API call 401'd and the shell layout 307'd on `fetchMe`; the factory now builds the real dual verifier when both are configured (`AlgDispatchVerifier`: protected-header `alg` HS256 → dev verifier, else JWKS — each branch verifies against its own key material only, so no downgrade: an HS256 token is accepted only if signed with `AUTH_DEV_SECRET`)                                                                                         | **CSV import execution round (PR #51, owner live-testing IMP-1/2/3).** (1) **Server-side bulk import:** `POST /contacts/import` (≤200 rows/call, zod contract in `packages/core/src/contact-import.ts`) replaces the per-row `POST /contacts` storm — one `withTenant` transaction per chunk: within-batch dedupe → case-insensitive workspace dedupe → suppression flagging (suppressed rows still create; A7 blocks at send) → batched custom-VALUE validation collected into `failed[]` BEFORE any write (a mid-tx create failure would poison the transaction) → creates (`source: "csv_import"`) → C2.8 list attach (archived lists never gain members) → post-commit `list.member.added.v1` events. This is also the seam the wizard CSV flow reuses (W3-1). (2) **Snapshot-at-review (IMP-2):** the Review tiles freeze when the user enters the step — the old `useMemo` recomputed against the 5s-polled `rows`, so the duplicates tile climbed as the import's own rows landed. The tiles are now labelled ESTIMATES; the done modal shows the server's authoritative counts, and the client makes NO skip decisions (every valid row goes up; the server re-dedupes transactionally), so stale poll data can no longer silently drop a legitimate row. (3) **Designed behavior change — within-batch duplicates:** two same-email rows in one file used to BOTH import (the old filter only checked existing contacts); now the first occurrence wins and later repeats count as `skippedDuplicates`. (4) **Execution states (IMP-1):** button disables on click → "Importing… X of N" + progress bar over 25-row chunks → done modal with real counts (imported/duplicates/suppressed/failed) or a designed error summary listing each failed row's email + reason with "Retry N failed" (failed rows only; a chunk is one transaction, so a network-failed chunk imported nothing and retry can never double-import). (5) **Close mid-import (owner: "pick one, log the DEC"):** closing the modal CONTINUES the import in the background and confirms via the §0 toast — sent chunks have already committed, so warn-and-abort could only strand a half-imported file; a caption under the progress bar says so. (6) Custom-field DEF creation stays the admin-gated client pre-step (C2.7 locks def-create to OWNER/ADMIN; import is any-member) — the endpoint takes custom VALUES only; flagged in the PR plan. (7) **51-review log line (owner-accepted, no code change):** the review-step estimate already compares LOWERCASED emails on both sides (snapshot builds the existing-set with `toLowerCase()` and lowercases each CSV email before the lookup), so client and server dedupe agree for ordinary case differences; the residual divergence is Postgres `mode: "insensitive"` unicode case-folding vs JS `toLowerCase()` on exotic characters (Turkish dotted-İ class) — accepted, since the done modal always renders the server's authoritative counts `ContactList`/`ListMembership` tables already existed (T1, RLS-policied, zero code references) — migration `20260708100000` adds the plan's semantics (`origin` backfilled `manual`, `archived`,                                                                                         | **Provider id vs RFC Message-ID split (P1.5 bug, caught by the P1.6 live-proof header gate, fix PR #31):** run | DEC-141 | 2026-08-31 | **A fact taught in settings is question → answer, and it reaches what Ada QUOTES.** The context spine is a keyed registry (`CONTEXT_FIELD_META`), so "Do you take my insurance?" had nowhere to live and nothing she quotes would carry the question. Three facts made the fix small: `contextFieldsSchema` is already an open record; `renderContextText` is the model's ONLY permitted fact source (DEC-015); and it falls back to the raw key for a label. So the value gains ONE optional `label`, that renderer prefers it, and a fact keyed `ask_<slug>` renders as `- ask_insurance (Do you take my insurance?): …`. Fields stored before this carry no label, so their rendered text is byte-identical — no migration, no new table, and "she knows it now" is a description rather than a toast. Answering a reported GAP writes the registry key directly instead, so the gap closes rather than sitting beside a near-duplicate. `field_*` keys are the same mechanism for a named field on Who you are; both prefixes are removable from this surface, registry keys are not. |

| DEC-150  | 2026-08-31 | **B6.5 ruling 1 — the lead-data provider is PLATFORM INFRASTRUCTURE, and consumer signal eligibility widens (ADDENDUM_5 §1–§2, owner amendment 2026-08-31).** One platform key, one vendor relationship, one bill we pay; the user pays in credits and never learns the vendor's name. So `provider not connected` is an OPERATOR condition and may not reach a user: the seam's own comment told callers to render it and now says the opposite, and Direct search reads "Search is temporarily unavailable · nothing for you to fix". **`SOURCE_ELIGIBILITY` widens to admit every supplier for every shape, superseding DEC-131 ruling 3's `consumer: ["first_party"]` ("consumer = first-party ONLY, ever")** — that was an over-absolute reading. | DEC-151  | 2026-08-31 | **B6.5 ruling 2 — the intent registry goes DEEP and WIDE (owner amendment + correction, 2026-08-31; the correction is authoritative).** A definition carried enough to sort a list, not enough to decide anything. `IntentSignalDef` now declares `subject` (person/organization — the org-first→person-second loop needs it), `supplier` + `basis` split out of the old single `source`, `tier` (`core`|`bp`), `confidence` with a multiplier so an inferred signal never scores like a witnessed one, `actionableForDays` — an outreach window DISTINCT from decay, pinned in test to be at least one half-life — `receiptSlots` with `slotDefaults`, `impliesGoal`/`impliesOffer` so intent feeds the DEC-114 next-best-action rules instead of only reordering, and `valueHint` so ranking can be revenue-weighted (ADDENDUM_2 §D). Added beside it: a **decay floor** below which a signal stops being SHOWN rather than lingering as noise, and the **combination + saturation + fatigue** table that did not exist (pair bonuses, a cap so eight weak signals never outrank one strong one, and a curve keyed to how often we already acted on this contact). **Receipts INTERPOLATE at write time** — the registry had always promised `{n}` while `intentReceipt()` returned the template verbatim, so every receipt read like a category ("hiring right now") instead of evidence ("posted 2 hygienist roles 3 days ago"); slots that carry grammatical weight declare a true generic fallback, because a slot that simply vanishes leaves a sentence limping. **WIDTH**: the prototype's six names are ONE demo workspace's examples, not the list — the taxonomy goes 11 → 20 types across every shape with `byVertical` vocabulary for dental, clinic, salon, fitness, legal, trades, real estate, saas, agency, ecommerce and education, plus user-facing GROUPS so the panel lists what a person recognises rather than our event keys. A vertical with no rows is a registry gap to fill, not a UI state to design. **NOT built, because the repo already has it** (the owner's correction, verified against the code): no negative-signal table — suppression ships in three layers (write-time in the consumer, a read-time pass in the controller, and `LeadExclusion`) and is kept; no provenance field — `IntentSignal.meta` already carries `{eventId, eventType}`; no schema change for subject — `contactId` and `companyKey` exist, only the DEFINITION lacked it; no cross-supplier identity dedupe, withdrawn as premature with one supplier live. **Two honesty corrections found by reviewing the frames**: `never_worked` rendered as "enquired once and never booked", asserting an enquiry a contact reached the book without ever making, and the group holding it repeated the claim — the type now says only what the record supports and moved to its own group. |

| DEC-158  | 2026-09-01 | **B9.5 — idempotency, and why `createMany` rather than insert-and-catch.** The key is `(workspaceId, sourceType, sourceId, reason)` behind a PARTIAL unique index — partial because manual adjustments carry no source and must stay unconstrained, as must every row written before the migration. Prisma cannot express a partial unique index, so it is raw SQL in the migration and documented on the model, the same workaround `BusinessContext`'s two-layer keys use. `sourceType`/`sourceId` are NEW columns rather than a reuse of `refId`, which already means the contact on a reveal and the AUDIT row on an adjustment. **Because we charge AFTER the thing happened, the produced row already exists and its id is the natural key** — a replayed webhook and a retried worker therefore leave exactly one row. The insert is `createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })`, and that is load-bearing rather than a style choice: in Postgres a unique violation ABORTS the surrounding transaction, so catching P2002 and continuing would leave the caller holding a poisoned tx where every later statement fails. `skipDuplicates` compiles to `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, which raises nothing, so a replay is an ordinary zero-row insert and `count === 0` means already-charged — a SUCCESS, since the work was paid for the first time round. Proven under concurrency, not just sequence: five simultaneous attempts on one source charge once. **Refunds are compensating POSITIVE rows** (`refund_<action>`, pointing at the same source) so the ledger stays append-only and a replayed bounce refunds once; soft bounces and complaints do not refund. |

## BusinessContext field registry (DEC-024, owner-approved 2026-07-03)

Semantics: **Required** = must be filled **with citations** from READY sources
(workspace or agent layer); uncited → gap row ("Type it" / "✦ Let AI"), step-6
launch gated. **Recommended** = distilled + cited when evidence exists; never
gaps, never blocks. Field keys are stable identifiers shared by the distiller,
gap checker, planner, and Brand kit.

**Core (required for every goal):** `offer` · `usp` · `tone`.

**Workspace-level required for any email goal:** `company_address` — the postal
address CAN-SPAM requires in every unsubscribe footer. Asked **once at
workspace level**, never per agent; usually auto-distilled + cited from the
website's contact/footer pages, so it only gaps when truly absent. **P1.5's
footer consumes this field — never a placeholder.**

| Goal card            | Required (gaps when uncited) — beyond core                                                   | Recommended (cited-if-found, never gaps)                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 📅 Book appointments | `icp` · `booking_link`                                                                       | `availability` (booking_link carries it — owner edit 1) · `pricing` · `proof_points` · `objection_handling`              |
| 🎯 Generate leads    | `icp`                                                                                        | `lead_magnet` (must not gate launch — owner edit 4) · `qualification_criteria` · `pricing` · `proof_points` · `services` |
| ♻ Reactivate leads   | `winback_offer` · `pricing` · `availability`                                                 | `relationship_context` · `proof_points`                                                                                  |
| 🚀 Drive sign-ups    | `icp` · `trial_details` · `pricing`                                                          | `proof_points` · `objection_handling`                                                                                    |
| ⭐ Collect reviews   | `review_channel` · `incentive_policy`                                                        | `services` · `tone` nuances for existing clients                                                                         |
| ✎ Custom goal        | core only, plus ≤2 distiller-proposed asks ("suggested for your goal", auditable, removable) | everything else                                                                                                          |

Owner edits applied (2026-07-03): (1) `availability` Required only on
Reactivate; (2) **`sender_identity` is NOT a context field** — the email
signature is a merge token resolved at send time from the step-5-selected
`SenderConnection`'s from-name; **P1.5 must FAIL a send whose sender lacks a
from-name** (never render a blank signature); (3) `company_address` added as
workspace-level Required for email goals; (4) `lead_magnet` → Recommended,
`qualification_criteria` added Recommended, `icp` stays Required on Generate
leads. Cross-cutting rules unchanged: `icp` not core; every field stored as
`{ value, citations: chunkId[], source: "distilled" | "typed" | "ai_decides" }`;
gap checker merges workspace+agent layers (agent wins, "✓ Found in your docs"
never re-asked, DEC-025); goal change re-runs gap evaluation (typed/delegated
answers persist; no-longer-required answers kept but ignored).

| Q-051                                                                                                                      | **Knowledge gap → Train Agent: the routing spec (SPEC A/DEC-099) — SPECIFIED, not open-ended (owner, 2026-07-26)** — the DETECTION half ships this unit: `call_knowledge_gap` fires when a live call hits an unanswerable question, and the `CallRetrieval` receipt already holds everything the row below needs. The ROUTING half is a queued unit, and the Train Agent surface itself is **not in the repo today** (Business Core → Train agent is console-v3 DESIGN, not shipped code; nothing implements it on main — verified). **It lands with the re-skin unit, which the owner is sequencing separately** (owner, 2026-07-26). **Owner-specified target shape — a call-detected gap lands in Train Agent as a PRE-POPULATED, UNGRADED row:** (a) **Question** = the caller's VERBATIM question from the receipt (`CallRetrieval.query`) — never a paraphrase; (b) **Answer** = the honest-absence line the agent ACTUALLY SPOKE — never a reconstruction of what it should have said. **THE JOIN IS EXPLICIT (owner amendment 2026-07-26, correcting the spec as first sent):** `answer` ← the VOICE TRANSCRIPT (`Message(channel:"voice", direction:"OUTBOUND")`), `searched facets` ← `CallRetrieval.emptyFacets`, **joined on `meta.callId`**. The receipt records what was LOOKED UP, not what was said; reading the answer off the receipt would yield a plausible-sounding reconstruction of the agent's line, which is exactly the failure this row exists to prevent. Both sides are already persisted — this is a query, not new plumbing; (c) **Source chips** = the facets that were searched and came back empty (`CallRetrieval.emptyFacets`); (d) **Provenance** = a `☎ from a live call` tag carrying date + campaign, so it is visibly distinct from an owner-typed test question; (e) it enters **UNGRADED**, so it flows into the EXISTING grade → "Teach her the right answer" → note/document path rather than a parallel one; (f) teaching it **writes back to knowledge exactly as a manual correction does** — no separate write path, no second ingestion route; (g) the **readiness score counts it like any other question**. That is what closes the loop this unit opens: a real customer asked something the agent couldn't answer, and the owner sees it where corrections already happen. **Second, smaller gap (unchanged):** `call_knowledge_gap` is not gated on voice connectivity in the picker (the `meeting_booked` precedent — always available). scatter, so this is the durable record of what each proof actually established
— not that it "passed", but what a reader may now rely on.

Degraded honestly when the saved `xoxb` predated `channels:read`: posted by channel NAME via `chat:write.public` and SAID so rather than guessing. |

The no-double-fire pin is the load-bearing result — `calendar.booked.v1` is the RECORD and the stage change is the trigger carrier, so rules, the Slack notifier and the goal machinery each fire once, not twice. |

The adversarial table caught a v4-mapped hex-form bypass before merge. |

Seven red runs first established four real HubSpot facts (write-only Service Key · EU regional host derived from the token prefix · `.test` TLD rejected · association refused by a per-account permission, NOT scope — identical before and after the read grant). |

Workspace suspension → `TENANT_SUSPENDED` in **5 ms**, restored in 24 ms. Agency suspension (cascading to its workspaces) → `TENANT_SUSPENDED` in **5 ms**, restored in 32 ms. Three consecutive runs gave a slowest stop of 7/7/9 ms — recorded because one run is not a measurement. Each row is a full cycle, not one assertion: a send that SUCCEEDED first (so the measurement is of traffic actually being stopped), the flip, the typed refusal, the clear, and a send that succeeded again — reversibility drilled because a stop nobody can undo is an outage, not a safety rail. The numbers are latency and not eventual consistency: `assertTenantActive`/`assertChannelLive` read per send with no cache or TTL. **Does not cover** a send already inside the SendGrid call — there is no cancel for a request in flight, and the exposure is one in-flight send per worker. Evidence: `docs/evidence/D1_KILL_SWITCH_DRILL.md`. |
